programme.title: Felix And Klara (7)
programme.desc: Klara juo aina vain enemmän, mutta Felix kieltäytyy tunnustamasta ongelmaa. Kun Felixin lehtikokoelma päätyy mukaan autokolariin, hän epäilee syylliseksi iäkästä naapuria.

programme.title: Felix And Klara (7)
programme.desc: Klara nostaa esiin läheisyyden puutteen ja toivoo, että heidän seksielämänsä olisi samanlaista kuin muillakin. Kun naapurissa asuva eläköitynyt kampaaja flirttailee Klaran kanssa, Felix tarttuu toimeen ja menee lääkäriin. Viagran sivuvaikutukset kuitenkin yllättävät.

programme.title: 10 kirjettä tulevaisuuteen (S)
programme.desc: Viruksen hallitessa maailmaa koululaiset ryhtyvät keräämään kirjeitä, jotka kapseloidaan yli 50 vuoden päästä avattaviksi. Päähenkilöt kirjoittavat kirjeensä ja puhuttelevat läheisiään tai jotakin tuntematonta tulevaisuudessa. Maailmanlaajuinen poikkeustila lävisti kaiken, mitä pidimme itsestään selvänä, ja sai monet arviomaan elämäänsä uudessa valossa. Dokumenttielokuva on kollektiivinen toteutus siitä, miten korona-pandemia ja poikkeustila näkyivät Suomessa. Pääohjaaja: Anu Kuivalainen (Suomi 2023)

programme.title: Ruoka-Suomi
programme.desc: Mykkä kansamme on syönyt jokapäiväisen leipänsä totisena, mutta nyt on uusi aika. Samae Koskinen kattaa ulkoilmaillallisen keskelle Helsinkiä, muistelee kouluruokaa ja käy psykologilla.

programme.title: Yliaika (7)
programme.desc: Suomi kukoistaa, mutta tiukoin ehdoin - kansalaisten on luovuttava oikeuksistaan 70-vuotiaina. Annastiina Kankaanrinta, entinen vaikutusvaltainen poliitikko, on ollut aikoinaan keskeisessä roolissa Lex 70 -lain luomisessa. Nyt, omana 70-vuotispäivänään, hänen on kohdattava oma exituksensa. Perustuu Piia Leinon romaaniin Yliaika.

programme.title: Elävä arkisto: Puukenkä - kesäkenkä (S)
programme.desc: Puupohjaisten korvikekenkien valmistus. (Finlandia-Kuva). (Mv)

programme.title: Gran Hotel (12)
programme.desc: Maite on vaarassa, ja Diego uhkuu vihaa. Mikä pelastaisi tilanteen? Ayala tietää hyvin kuka valehtelee, mutta miksi ja miten se todistetaan? Andrés on kahden naisen loukussa. Teresa odottaa myötäjäisiä.

programme.title: La Promesa - Salaisuuksien kartano (12)
programme.desc: Samuel yrittää vakuuttaa Marían siitä, että Carlolle pitäisi antaa mahdollisuus olla lapsensa isä. Leocadia yrittää tehdä sovinnon Margaritan kanssa. Mitkä ovat Curron ja Ángelan suunnitelmat?

programme.title: Lewerentz - elämän ja kuoleman arkkitehti
programme.desc: Ruotsalainen Sigurd Lewerentz (1885 - 1975) on yksi arvostetuimmista ja myyttisimmistä arkkitehdeistä. Hänen suunnittelemiaan rakennuksia ja alueita kuten Skogskyrkogårdenin hautausmaata rakastetaan, mutta kuka oli julkisuudesta poissa pysytellyt Sigurd Lewerentz? Se paljastui, kun kellarista löytyi 16 mm kuvanauhoja ja äänitteitä, joissa tapamme myyttisen Sigurd Lewerentzin ensimmäistä kertaa. Ohjaus: Sven Blume. (Lewerentz - Divine Darkness, Ruotsi 2023)

programme.title: Elokuvan hetki: Hetki ennen valoa (S)
programme.desc: Arjen hiljaiset sankarit - Klaus Härö humaanien tarinoiden kertojana. Hetki ennen valoa -elokuvassa kahden naisen tarinat risteävät hoitoalan kriisin keskiössä. Klaus Härö kertoo elokuvan idean alkuvaiheista ja Laura Birn valmistautumisestaan Inkan rooliin.

programme.title: 100 ruudutonta päivää
programme.desc: Vieroitushoito jatkuu, ja Erik Galli ottaa nyt seuraavan askeleen kohti tasapainoista suhdetta ruutuihin. Sosiaalinen media on tästedes kielletty, ja peruspuhelimen kanssa elämisessä on omat haasteensa. Psykiatri ja Erikin mentori Anders Hansen yrittää yhdessä Erikin uusien ja vanhojen ystävien kanssa tukea häntä vieroituksessa. Erik pääsee näkemään, miten internet- ja teknologiariippuvaiset nuoret saavat apua hoitokodissa.

programme.title: Livet - suomenruotsalaisia tarinoita
programme.desc: Nyt lähdetään tutkimusmatkalle jäätikköluolaan. Fredrik Aspö rakastaa uusien paikkojen löytämistä - mieluiten sellaisten, joihin ei pääse ihan helposti. Hän uskoo saaneensa syntymässä tutkimusmatkailijan geenit. Juuri ne ovat vieneet hänet Sipoon tasamailta Pohjois-Norjan tuntureille.

programme.title: Hääkuvaajat
programme.desc: Hääkuvaaja Maria Broström tapaa morsiamen, joka suunnittelee häitä salaa. Edes mies ei vielä tiedä, että häntä kositaan hääpäivän aamuna. Ruotsalaisessa sarjassa seurataan hääkuvaajien työtä. Osa 3/6. (Bröllopsfotograferna, T: SVT, 2022).

programme.title: Vuoroviikoin
programme.desc: Malenan huoltajuuskiista vaikuttaa koko hänen arkeensa. Miten luoda perhe, kun vanhat mallit eivät riitä? Wilma ja Perttu kokeilevat uutta vuoroviikkojärjestelyä. Janica kipuilee etäsuhteen kanssa, ja Jenny etsii rauhaa kylpylästä.

programme.desc: Viimeisimmät uutiset, uutisanalyysit ja reportaasit ruotsinkieliseltä rannikkoseudulta, muualta Suomesta ja maailmalta.

programme.title: Milloin voin lentää vihreästi?
programme.desc: Moni lentää aurinkolomalleen. Poliitikot lupaavat, että lentokoneiden päästöistä päästään eroon. Kuinka kestävä ratkaisu paistorasvalla lentäminen on? Ovatko sähköpolttoaineet, akut vai vety tulevaisuuden ratkaisuja? Lähde ruotsalaisen dokumenttielokuvan mukaan salaisiin lentokonehalleihin, joissa tulevaisuuden ympäristöystävällinen lentoliikenne on valmiina valloittamaan ilmatilan.

programme.title: Efter Nio
programme.desc: Linda Sällström on jättänyt ammattilaisjalkapallon ja ahtaa nyt jalkansa liian pieniin tanssikenkiin. Jaana Henriksson ja Kjell Wallenius kokivat Estonian katastrofin ensimmäiseltä kannelta. Nino Poppius on matkustanut mystikon Ior Bockin jalanjäljissä. Sonja ja Janne päättivät pyöräillä töihin, noin 80 kilometrin matkan.

programme.title: Ihmeiden äärellä (12)
programme.desc: Kun kaksivuotias Konstantin saa vakavan diagnoosin, Jerry joutuu eettisen ongelman eteen, ja päätyy avoimeen konfliktiin Lindan kanssa. Lasse turhautuu siitä, ettei hänellä ole tarpeeksi aikaa potilaille. Raju yhteenotto isän kanssa pakottaa Jerryn kohtaamaan sen, mitä hän on yrittänyt piilottaa. Frederik joutuu pulaan.

programme.title: Vasikka (12)
programme.desc: Hän myy huumeita Foxtrot-verkoston laskuun, mutta kieltäytyy auttamasta jengipomon sukulaisen murhassa. Veristen tapahtumien seuratessa toisiaan hän kääntyy poliisin puoleen. Jäädessään kahden palkkamurhaajan seuraan hänen täytyy vain luottaa siihen, että poliisi tulee väliin. Tosikuvaus jengiläisestä, josta tuli vasikka.

programme.title: Orgasmitakuu (16)
programme.desc: Uudenlainen naisten seksilelu on saanut aikaan suoranaisen globaalin itsetyydytysvallankumouksen. Ympäri Ruotsia asuvat naiset kertovat dokumentissa kokemuksistaan vibraattorista, jolla sanotaan olevan orgasmitakuu. Monilla ohjelman naisista onkin läheisempi suhde seksileluunsa kuin kumppaniinsa. Mikä tämän uudenlaisen vibraattorin salaisuus on? Entä voiko itsetyydytystä harjoittaa liikaa? Dokumentti itsetyydytyksen iloista. Tuotanto: SVT.

programme.title: Avara luonto: Irlannin kivinen ihme
programme.desc: Irlannin länsirannikolla sijaitsee Burrenin kansallispuisto, joka tunnetaan ainutlaatuisesta kalkkikivitasangostaan. Tämä luonnonihme on myös koti monille villieläimelle ja kasveille. Ohjelmassa tutustutaan tähän poikkeukselliseen alueeseen, jossa näkyy myös ihmisen kädenjälki. (Green Island, Grey Desert, Tuotanto: Crossing the Line/ORF/ARTE/PBS, Irlanti 2024).

programme.title: Perjantai-dokkari: Lapsi, joka halusi pois saaresta
programme.desc: Ei tää sit ollutkaan niin iso paikka, sanoo ulkosaaristossa asuva 10-vuotias Viljami. Lapsuus Utön saaressa tarkoittaa seikkailuja, mutta myös kaipuuta suurempaan. Ohjaaja Saara Tuominen.

programme.title: Kansallismaisemat: Lappia
programme.desc: Maisemakuvia Lapista, kuvattu kesällä 2004.

programme.title: Ykkösaamu
programme.desc: Yleisradio viettää 100-vuotisjuhliaan. Miten julkisen palvelun verovaroin rahoitettu mediayhtiö jaksaa alan myllerryksessä? Ykkösaamun vieraana on Ylen toimitusjohtaja Marit af Björkesten. Seija Vaaherkumpu haastattelee.

programme.title: Koko Suomen viikko
programme.desc: Viikon kiinnostavimmat paikalliset uutiset, ilmiöt ja puheenaiheet ympäri maata.

programme.title: Flinkkilä And Kellomäki
programme.desc: Avaruustähtieteen professori halusi lapsena olla Marsin sotavaltias ja kirjailija haaveili Ihmemaan Liisan tunnelista. Anne Flinkkilän vieraana Emmi Itäranta ja Esko Valtaoja.

programme.title: Jumalanpalvelus
programme.desc: Kanssasi maailmalla. Suomen Merimieskirkon 150-vuotismessu Helsingin tuomiokirkosta. Saarnaa piispa Jukka Keskitalo, liturgina Maria Obafemi-Onuigbo, musiikissa Viva Vox ja Laivaston soittokunnan kvintetti, kanttoreina Inka Kinnunen ja Anu Pulkkinen. Suomen Merimieskirkko perustettiin auttamaan suomalaisia merimiehiä ulkomailla, mutta jo varsin pian siirtolaisista ja matkailijoista tuli suurimpia asiakasryhmiä. Ulkomailla suomalaisia merimieskirkkoja on tällä hetkellä neljä, Suomessa seitsemän. Yksi asia on pysynyt: ihmisen kohtaaminen.

programme.title: Tuhkimotarinoita
programme.desc: Synnytettyään kuolleen lapsen Kati pisti välit poikki kroppansa kanssa. Keho oli pettänyt hänet! Palautuuko yhteys kehoon tanssilla, ja mitä hän sanoo, kun kesken tanssin saliin astelee Juha Tapio? O: Mape Morottaja.

programme.title: Urheilulukio
programme.desc: Davin valmistautuu arvokisoihin ja Nellie on uuden äärellä, kun kova työ palkitaan. Aada juhlii synttäreitään ja Eero jatkaa uuden joukkueen etsintää

programme.title: Lomittajat (7)
programme.desc: Anne A. osallistuu vasikoiden nupoutukseen, kotona kanalassa kukonpoikien päivät ovat luetut. Anne S:n lempilehmä saa poikimahalvauksen ja eläinlääkäriä tarvitaan nopeasti apuun. Anna-Maija työskentelee sikalassa yhdessä puolisonsa Arin kanssa. Kotiin on kiva palata, siellä odottaa maailman ihanin koira Viima. Aki puolestaan viettää juhannusviikon laulukeikoilla ympäri Suomen. Kaksi eri ammattia, kaksi vahvaa rakkautta.

programme.title: Akuutti: Masentuneen rinnalla
programme.desc: Joel ja Ida Kallio menivät naimisiin nelisen vuotta sitten. Pariskunnan odotuksissa oli iloinen, läheinen ja rakkauden täyteinen liitto, mutta pian liittoon astui mukaan Idan masennus. Miten terveen puolison tulisi tukea sairastunutta uupumatta itse? Anne Lindgrenin veli sairastui masennukseen koulukiusaamisen takia. Sisarukset olivat läheisiä, mutta juuri kun kaikki näytti hyvältä, teki pikkuveli itsemurhan. Voiko traumaattisesta kokemuksesta koskaan toipua? Toimittaja Risto Kuusisto.

programme.title: Velipuolikuu (7)
programme.desc: Länkkärileffa Yksi mies, yksi nainen. Aforismeja - kuten Keho, tuo tekstiilien temmellyskenttä. Lahtinen palaa maan pinnalle. Appivanhemmat vierailulla. Elaine Altain vuorilla.

programme.title: Kerro, kerro kuvasta (S)
programme.desc: Jenny Yen eli tubettaja Jennysvoices lapsuudessa tärkeintä oli leikki ja erityisesti nukkekoti- ja roolileikit. Lapsena hän kävi puheterapiassa useiden eri äänteiden vuoksi. Myöhemmin hän huomasi leikin luoneen hänelle mielikuvitusrikkaan äänimaailman, jota hän alkoi hyödyntämään ääninäyttelijän töissä.

programme.title: Pikku Kakkonen And BUU-klubben: 100-vuotissynttärit - 100 årskalas
programme.desc: Pikku Kakkosen ja BUU-klubbenin rakastetuimmat hahmot ja juontajat kerääntyvät juhlimaan 100-vuotissynttäreitä täyden Helsingin areenan lavalle. Pikku Kakkosen Leikkiorkesteri lyö tahdit ja kompit juhlaan, joka on täynnä laulua ja leikkiä.

programme.title: Monsen ja kansallispuistot
programme.desc: Monsen etsii rauhaa ja selvittää, miksi juuri tämä metsä on niin arvokas. Tänä vuonna luontoterapia on hänelle tärkeämpää kuin koskaan.

programme.title: Game of Wool - suuri lankasota
programme.desc: Tekstuuriviikolla kilpailijat luovat syötävän hyviä neuleita, eli toisin sanoen ruokaa. Amigurumeiksi sanotut neuleet haastavat kisaajat, joiden pitää taikoa lautaselle lempiruokansa mahdollisimman realistisena. Luomuksissa nähdään mm. pekonia, kananmunia ja paahtopaistia. Joukkuehaasteessa valmistetaan pareittain paksusta langasta neuletakkeja, joiden pitää olla mukavia ja näyttäviä.

programme.title: Anne ja Anders Bhutanissa
programme.desc: Bhutan on herättänyt maailman huomion omalla määritelmällään merkityksellisestä elämästä. Pienessä buddhalaisessa valtiossa onni, henkinen hyvinvointi ja kulttuuriset arvot asetetaan talouskasvun edelle. Anne ja Anders matkustavat Bhutaniin kokeakseen itse, mistä on kysymys. Heti saapumisen jälkeen Anne vierailee erityisessä koulussa, jossa tunne-elämän tasapaino on yhtä tärkeää kuin varsinainen oppiminen. Anders tapaa maan pääministerin sekä tanskalaisen Larsin, joka tuntee onnellisuutta vaalivan maan harvinaisen hyvin.

programme.title: Tulennielijä (7)
programme.desc: Helena tapaa yöllä nuhruisessa kapakassa pienen tytön, jonka isä kerää kaljarahansa laulattamalla tyttöä ryyppykavereilleen. Helena säälii tyttöä ja auttaa häntä esiintymään. Tyttö kiintyy pelastajaansa ja lähtee seuraamaan Helenaa.

programme.title: Mieheni vaimo (12)
programme.desc: Menestynyt liikemies Ahti Kariluoto saa Tallinnan laivalla sydänkohtauksen. Sairaalassa kaksi naista kohtaavat ja miehen vuosia kestänyt kaksoiselämä paljastuu.

programme.title: Ilmastoaktivistin päiväkirja
programme.desc: Laura käynnistää kunnianhimoisen kampanjan herättääkseen suomalaiset uhkaavaan ilmastokriisiin. Samalla testataan miten pitkälle nuoren naisen voimavarat riittävät taistelussa ilmastonmuutosta vastaan. O: Nina Malmberg

programme.title: Peltsin kova vuosi
programme.desc: Mikä on Peltsin heikko kohta - pystysuora kallioseinämä, ahdas luola vai kuohuva koski? Kovan vuoden kuvaaja Juha Korhonen laati Peltsille haasteen, josta ei pelkällä fysiikalla selviä.

programme.title: Becoming Led Zeppelin (12)
programme.desc: Dokumentti Led Zeppelinin perustamisesta ja noususta maailman kuumimmaksi rockbändiksi 60-luvun lopussa. Robert Plant, Jimmy Page ja John Paul Jones kertovat lapsuudestaan sodanjälkeisessä Britanniassa ja tapaamisestaan 1968. Vuonna 1980 kuollut John Bonham on mukana ääninauhalla, jota ei ole kuultu aiemmin. Ohjelmassa on runsaasti ennen julkaisematonta videomateriaalia yhtyeen alkuaikojen keikoilta Englannista ja Yhdysvalloista. (Becoming Led Zeppelin, Britannia 2025)

programme.title: Esine 817 (7)
programme.desc: Uralilla eristyneen kylän asukkaat kertovat Neuvostoliiton ensimmäisestä ydinonnettomuudesta, joka tapahtui alueella vuonna 1957. Onnettomuus peitettiin, koska lähellä oleva ydinvoimala valmisti ydinaseita. Kyläläisistä, jotka elivät radioaktiivisella maalla, tuli hallituksen salaisuuksien vankeja. Hiljaisuus synnytti tarinoita, kuten mutatoituneesta sikiöstä, joka muuttui muukalaislegendaksi ja sai muistomerkin.

programme.title: Avoimena
programme.desc: Kokeakseen itsensä arvokkaaksi Amalie tarvitsee kipeästi vahvistusta muilta. Hän käyttää päivänsä rakentamalla instagramiin mielikuvaa siitä, että kaikki on hyvin. Sen taakse Amalie voi kätkeä yksinäisyyden ja epävarmuuden tunteitaan. Onnistuuko Amalie löytämään rauhan itsensä kanssa vai onko hänen loputtomiin haettava toisilta hyväksyntää?

programme.desc: Kokelaiden tehtävänä on pelastaa nukke pilkkopimeästä asunnosta ennen kuin happi loppuu. Lisäksi heitä odottaa kaoottinen linja-auto-onnettomuusharjoitus, joka panee heidän hermonsa ja nopeutensa koetukselle.

programme.desc: Vanhan metsän ainutlaatuinen asukki.

programme.desc: Tarinoita metsästä kertoo suomalaisen metsäluonnon kauneudesta ja esittelee monimuotoisen vanhan metsän luontoa sekä asukkaita lyhyiden, tietopitoisten kertomusten muodossa. Ohjaus: Kim Saarniluoto. Tuotanto: Matila Röhr Nordisk Oy.

programme.title: Norja veden alla
programme.desc: Unelmien matka alkaa olla lopuillaan. Viimeisenä etappina on Finnmarken. Ystävykset pääsevät vielä kokemaan kuningasrapujen hyökkäyksen. Suuri yllätys on myös se, kun valtavat määrät etelänkiisloja kerääntyy paikalle.

programme.title: Tiettömän taipaleen takana
programme.desc: Trond Henning Monan asuu pienessä majassa veden äärellä. Nuorimies eli ennen vaeltelevaa elämää, kunnes löysi lopulta elämälleen rauhan ja mielekkyyden Kristiansandin lähimetsästä.

programme.title: Tanskalainen maajussi
programme.desc: Sisäänkäynnin värjätty betonilattia viimeistellään. Frank maalaa kärryn rungon ja pyörät ja nikkaroi puusta uuden lavan. Yksi karitsoista päätyy pakastimeen.

programme.title: Minun maisemani
programme.desc: Norjalaiset liikkuvat mielellään luonnossa. Kaupunkien ympäristöissäkin on runsaasti nähtävää. Tänään tutustutaan Bergenin maisemiin.

programme.title: Taiteilijasiirtokunta Hornbækissa
programme.desc: Taiteilijat vierailevat Nivaagaards Malerisamling -taidemuseossa, jonne heidän näyttelynsä tulee. Keskustelu taiteen seksismistä käy kiivaana. Christian maalaa naturistin, ja Noah lähtee juhlimaan kalastajien kanssa.

programme.title: Talot huokuvat historiaa
programme.desc: Anna ja Mats asuvat talossa, jonka historia pitää sisällään suuria tunteita. Talo sijaitsee vanhalla vuorimiestilalla Vilkesbackassa Falunin lähellä. Talon yläkerrassa on huone, jonka hirsiseinät on koristeltu käsinmaalatuin kukkasin. Antiikkiesineiden tuntija Rickard Thunér auttaa perhettä selvittämään pitävätkö vanhat tarinat paikkansa. Niiden mukaan eräs talon piika tappoi vastasyntyneen lapsensa ja hautasi hänet kuistin portaiden alle. Rakennustutkija Erika Åberg auttaa tapetoimaan yhden huoneen perinteikkäässä talossa.

programme.title: Pikku Kakkonen
programme.desc: Katsellaan Tuomon kanssa Albi Lumiukko, Ihan mahtava luonto, Arvaa kuinka paljon sinua rakastan, Dalin leikkiseikkailut, Herää sukka sekä Muru.

programme.title: Timanttinen keikka
programme.desc: Laulaja Erin esiintyy Timanttisella keikalla yhtyeineen ja luo G-Livelabin lavalla intiimin ja koskettavan tunnelman. Erinin energia kannattelee keikkaa vaivattomasti ja esityksen herkkä jännite pitää yleisöä hyppysissään ja säilyy loppuun saakka.

programme.title: Teatterikorkea - näyttämölle valitut
programme.desc: Teatterikorkeakoulun syksy käynnistyy protestimielialassa. Näyttelijäopiskelijat Nomi ja Aapo aloittavat Elina Knihtilän vetämän monologikurssin, jossa rima nousee taivaisiin. Samalla on haussa roolit musikaalissa ja tv-sarjassa. Tanssinopiskelijoiden Miskan ja Eliaksen arkea hämmentää vieraileva opettaja Thomas.

programme.title: Eränkävijät
programme.desc: Kausi 8. 9/12. Mehtämikon odotukset uudesta vaellusreitistä ovat vaihtelevat. Jäätyneistä varusteista huolimatta retkikeittiön antimet lämmittävät mieltä. Myös Pohjois-Karjalassa ollaan suksien päällä. Mikko ja Kaitsu suuntaavat kanalintujahtiin, ja tilanteita riittää heti reissun alkumetreiltä lähtien. Manu ja Aleksi ovat lähteneet etsimään pilkkijäitä rannikolta. Kalaonnen takaamiseksi takataskussa on tuttuun tapaan innovatiivisia ideoita. Myös Marjo ja Pinja ovat lähteneet pilkkiretkelle, jonka aikana Pinja pääsee yöpymään ensimmäistä kertaa lumikuopassa.

programme.title: Game of Wool - suuri lankasota
programme.desc: Nyt ei puutu kisasta säihkettä ja ylellisyyttä! Viiden jäljellä olevan kilpailijan tehtävänä on valmistaa langasta näyttävä kaksiosainen korusetti, joka kelpaisi vaikka kuninkaallisille. Joukkuekisassa tehdään lampunvarjostin, jonka pitää koostua viidestä identtisestä paneelista. Tarkkuus ja viimeistelyjälki korostuvat, kun virheille ei ole enää varaa.

programme.title: Kelsey Cook: Mark Your Territory
programme.desc: Kelsey Cook recently relocated to Minnesota in the dead of winter to move in with her boyfriend. She covers the perks of dating an older man, the chaos of IUD insertions, navigating a parent with dementia, and much more.

programme.title: Matt Rife: Matthew Steven Rife
programme.desc: In his second self-produced hour special, built by friends and fans, Matt pushes comedic boundaries with stories, improv, and positive messages. A charismatic look into his wit, sharp humor, and crowd-driven energy.

programme.title: Kyle Kinane: Dirt Nap
programme.desc: Kinane explores tolerance and returning to his roots with self-deprecating humor, mining comedy from his suburban life after years on the road — from vegan quesadillas to the Fast and Furious franchise to life with a wayward cat.

programme.title: Matt Rife: Only Fans
programme.desc: Matt Rife's debut stand-up special, a culmination of his first ten years doing comedy starting at age 15. Fan-funded and self-produced, it showcases his sharp crowd work, edgy humor, and personal storytelling.

programme.desc: With their first child on the way, Deb and Tony move in Atchison, Kansas. But when their son is born, the child's toys seem to take on a life of their own and strange whispers torment Tony.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In Brookfield, Connecticut, young David suffers from intense nightmares and is physically attacked by an invisible entity. Paranormal investigators make contact with a legion of demons inside the child's body.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: An enigmatic photo of her boyfriend's brother killed in Vietnam entrances Lisa. As her obsession grows, she realizes that the spirit of the dead soldier is taking control of their lives.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In a small house in Glen Burnie, Maryland, unseen intruders attack 10-year-old Billy Bean. Billy struggles to learn the secrets of the house and fight them in any way he can - to save his sanity.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: When Clara and her family move into a small home in rural Hinsdale, New York, they realize that the peace of life in the country is merely an illusion - and the threat of death is very real.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Ed and Beth's ranch house seems like the perfect place to raise their toddler until they discover that they are not alone. A dark, heavy mist hangs over the house and grows larger day by day.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: When Selena and her 3-year-old son move into an old house in Michigan, a series of photographs show what she cannot see with the naked eye: an evil face in the attic.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: After Mike and his girlfriend Lisa move in their new house, Lisa's personality begins to change dramatically.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Randy recites an incantation from a book on witchcraft, hoping to make contact with spirits of the dead.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: The Fahey family has lived in the same townhouse in the city of Galway, Irelan, for decades. But when a new baby arrives, he stirs up the psychic energy of a terrible crime committed many years ago.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: The new owners know that there is something strange about the Wheatsheaf Pub in Northern England. Behind the walls, they find bits of clothing and bones. Then, the pub itself begins to attack those within.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Mary Vogel has been a spiritual counselor for ten years, but a recent encounter with the demonic forces her to question everything she knows and trusts. Only an exorcism can save her soul.

programme.title: mareTV: Martinique
programme.desc: The island of Martinique is a piece of France in the Caribbean, between Florida and South America. And of course, Savoir-vivre applies just as it does on the other side of the Atlantic, between the English Channel and the Mediterranean. Jacky Pascault is the first and only man to cultivate mushrooms in the Caribbean. Everywhere else, they grow on artificially fertilised soil, but Jacky's Champignons Tropicaux flourish on sugar cane fibres. Nicole Vilo tailors hats and dresses out of coconut palms. Of course, the catwalk for the models wearing her first collection is one of the countless dream beaches. The Martiniquais sail on boats they call Yole, which have no keel and are therefore difficult to navigate. The crew members hang over the water in breakneck fashion on long wooden poles. Just the job for Yole-boss Max' problem kids: they not only learn complicated handling, but also team spirit.

programme.title: glCuba - Brilliantly Caribbean
programme.desc: Even anyone who has not yet been to Cuba can conjure up certain images of American vintage street cruisers, imposing buildings that have seen better days, white sandy beaches full of palms and loving couples on the Malecón against a backdrop of crashing waves. This island is somewhat of a myth and its people generate a special joie de vivre. The legendary Hershey Train departs for Matanzas from the capital, Havana. On the oldest electrified railway line in the Caribbean, 60-year-old Spanish carriages make their way along al-most 100 kilometres of coastline in the most relaxed way possible. The Salvavidas on Varadero, probably the most famous beach on the island, have a particular-ly beautiful workplace. The lifeguards' territory ex-tends for more than 20 kilometres. In order to protect the coasts of Cuba, mangroves have been replanted here for many years. The project is supported by the UN and planting is often carried out by schoolchildren. In doing so, Cuban children learn how to treat their maritime habitat in a sustainable fashion. The former colonial city of Trinidad on Cuba's south coast is gen-erally considered to be one of the most beautiful places in the entire Caribbean. The houses here are particular-ly colourful. A plethora of magnificent buildings can be seen at the Plaza Mayor, the neo-baroque main square.

programme.title: Caribbean sisters: The Lesser Antilles St. Kitts And Nevis
programme.desc: In the centre of the Caribbean, volcanoes rise steeply from the sea, thus shaping the sister islands of St. Kitts And Nevis. Their slopes, covered in lush rainforests, snow-white, sandy beaches and the surrounding tur-quoise tinted waters provide the ultimate setting for this record-breaking, albeit tiny island paradise: Both islets are the smallest of the Caribbean dwarf states and also rank among the world’s ten smallest states. A hot pepper sauce, made of a creative mixture of ginger, garlic, thyme and extraordinarily hot chillies that thrive in the hot and humid climate of Nevis, is simmering on the stove of Violet and Llewellyn’s house. Lemmy Pemberton digs up abandoned turtle nests with his bare hands, as he wants to be certain that all of the babies have indeed managed to make it. Members of the Turtle Group catch sea turtles in order to take their measurements and fit them with transmitters. Taxi bus-es are not only the main means of transport on St. Kitts And Nevis, they are also an artistic expression of each driver’s personality. Colourfully embellished, each taxi represents island art on wheels.

programme.title: The Heart of Hawaii - The Island of Oahu
programme.desc: The Oahu island is the economic and cultural centre of the Hawaiian archipelago, as well as being a paradise for surfers, active holidaymakers and freedom lovers. The island is home to more than half of all natives and almost eight million foreign guests annually. Anyone searching for peace and seclusion won’t find either in Honolulu or Waikiki. Traffic congestion and a backdrop of skyscrapers belong to the town panorama. Hip cafes, galleries and young fashion firms have settled here, adding a new and modern flair to the capital. Cindy’s Lei Shoppe, the Chinatown florists, has been here for more than 30 years. This is also because the so-called Leis, the tradition of floral decoration, usually offered as a flower necklace or as a headdress, is still an important part of Hawaiian culture. Keone Nunes is well-known for his traditional tattooing skills, whereby the so-called Kakau Tattoos are virtually hammered into the skin with a hippo tooth. But Oahu is also an island of overwhelming natural beauty and a fascinating diversity on the smallest of places ...

programme.title: The Seychelles - Africa with South Seas ambience
programme.desc: The 115 islands and islets that make up the Seychelles present a breath-taking variety of plants, rare animals and beaches laced with palms. This is where the leg-endary Coco de Mer palm nuts grow with fruits weigh-ing up to 20 kilos and giant wild land turtles nibble away at mangrove fruits to their hearts content. The archipelago was first settled at the end of the 18th cen-tury. Today, a very colourful potpourri of peoples in this dwarf state proves just how peacefully different cultures can live side by side. Three times a week, the steamer MV Espoir completes the trip from the main island of Mahé to Praslin and back. A ship for every-one and practically everything: Used cars, toilet paper, horses, bicycles, furniture - you name it, the Espoir transports goods of all kinds. Coconuts sometimes pose a problem as there are far too many of them. What to do with them? The best place to send them is undoubt-edly Hubert Roumien's Virgin Coconut Oil Laboratory, hidden away in the Mahé jungle. Straw turns into gold at Seaweed Seychelles! There, Benjamin Port Louis collects seaweed and extracts liquid fertiliser from it.

programme.title: mareTV: The Caribbean for explorers: St. Vincent and the Grenadines
programme.desc: Much more Caribbean than on the islands of St. Vincent and the Grenadines is hardly possible. Deserted beaches, uninhabited islands, lush vegetation, the 33 islands in total are dreamlike with extremely hospitable inhabitants. Miranda Phillips runs a laundry and water boat on Bequia. Every morning, the 32-year-old navigates from yacht to yacht with her small bright green service vehicle and is already expected by most skippers. Miranda promises radiantly fresh laundry, which she delivers again the same day. And so there is always something going on in her tiny laundrette in the harbour. It turns into a karaoke bar in the evening, because that is Miranda's great passion. Eban Olliver has many jobs at once. He is the lighthouse keeper of Kingstown. And that means a lot of responsibility in St. Vincent's biggest port city. Because Eban doesn't just change the light bulbs, he's a pilot dispatcher, harbour master and guard all in one person. First contact with ships is particularly important. Once he even saved the entire nation from an Ebola virus.

programme.title: mareTV: Mexico's Caribbean Coast
programme.desc: The palm tree laden beaches on Mexico's Riviera Maya on the Yucatan peninsula are endless, and the turquoise sea with its gentle Caribbean surf is a warm 25 degrees during the mild winter in this part of the world. Between Cancún and Punta Allen, where once there was little more than bushland and a few sleepy fishing villages, vibrant life has evolved during the past three decades. Richard Sowa has lived on a floating island for the past 15 years: an island he built himself out of empty plastic bottles. The bon vivant him-self sees it as a solution for our planet's refuse problem. Off Punta Allen, a village in the bay of Sian Ka'an, Mexican Mara Coral Ley and her cousin Kim, continue to catch lobsters by adhering to the traditional method and were awarded an Eco seal for sustainable fishing for their trouble. It is silent under water off Isla Mujeres and it is here that the artist Jason deCaires has constructed a sculpture park. Hundreds of lifesize figures form an artificial reef at a depth of 12 metres. Fish and plants complete his work of art. The master himself is convinced: Mother Nature is the true artist.

programme.title: mareTV: Curacao, Blue Wonder of the Caribbean
programme.desc: Curacao is one of the most popular attractions for countless cruise ships on their trips through the Caribbean, because it is located outside of the hurricane belt. This is why Eric Miguel is constantly in action. He is the bridge keeper of the Queen Emma Bridge, the landmark of Curacao's capital, Willemstad. After his shift, Eric goes to Yvonne Troeman's cook-shop. Her speciality is Kadushi, a cactus soup. The ingredients include cactus flesh, pigtail's, mussels and a few secret treats. Barbara van Bebber is the only submarine pilot on Curacao and literally gets to the bottom of things amidst the turquoise-blue wonder of the Caribbean. She charters out her sub to marine biologists and wealthy private explorers, simultaneously cleaning up on the seabed. Her Curasub has claw arms, which she employs to remove anything that doesn't belong down there: beer bottles, car tyres, and plastic refuse. Jeroen Eikelenboom simply carts sand from a neighbouring cove to his own surf club in his favourite bay.

programme.title: Sri Lanka - Tropics, temples and tea plantations
programme.desc: Sri Lanka stands for colourful diversity in all respects. If it's spirituality or Ayurveda you're looking for, here it is. Adventurers and nature lovers can also satisfy their needs here. No one must travel far to discover exotic worlds on this drop-shaped tropical island. mareTV delves into the day to day lives of the is-landers, some of whom pursue the most unusual pro-fessions: Uditha Lakmaal is a palm tree climber. He harvests the sap of the trees, known as palm wine, by climbing to the top of them. Sri Lankan stilt fishermen now actually have very little to do with fish and func-tion more as models receiving payment from tourists for acting the part. Anulawathie runs a small floating hoop business, offering car inner tubes for adults and tuk-tuk tubes for children. Different varieties of tea can be found on Herman Gunaratnes tea plantation. Just four carefully selected women are allowed to harvest the exclusive white tea grown there. Each tea leaf is cut individually from the bush by gloved hands and with golden scissors.

Of course, the catwalk for the models wearing her first collection is one of the countless dream beaches. The Martiniquais sail on boats they call Yole, which have no keel and are therefore difficult to navigate. The crew members hang over the water in breakneck fashion on long wooden poles. Just the job for Yole-boss Max' problem kids: they not only learn complicated handling, but also team spirit.

programme.title: glCuba - Brilliantly Caribbean
programme.desc: Even anyone who has not yet been to Cuba can conjure up certain images of American vintage street cruisers, imposing buildings that have seen better days, white sandy beaches full of palms and loving couples on the Malecón against a backdrop of crashing waves. This island is somewhat of a myth and its people generate a special joie de vivre. The legendary Hershey Train departs for Matanzas from the capital, Havana. On the oldest electrified railway line in the Caribbean, 60-year-old Spanish carriages make their way along al-most 100 kilometres of coastline in the most relaxed way possible. The Salvavidas on Varadero, probably the most famous beach on the island, have a particular-ly beautiful workplace. The lifeguards' territory ex-tends for more than 20 kilometres. In order to protect the coasts of Cuba, mangroves have been replanted here for many years. The project is supported by the UN and planting is often carried out by schoolchildren. In doing so, Cuban children learn how to treat their maritime habitat in a sustainable fashion. The former colonial city of Trinidad on Cuba's south coast is gen-erally considered to be one of the most beautiful places in the entire Caribbean. The houses here are particular-ly colourful. A plethora of magnificent buildings can be seen at the Plaza Mayor, the neo-baroque main square.

programme.title: Caribbean sisters: The Lesser Antilles St. Kitts And Nevis
programme.desc: In the centre of the Caribbean, volcanoes rise steeply from the sea, thus shaping the sister islands of St. Kitts And Nevis. Their slopes, covered in lush rainforests, snow-white, sandy beaches and the surrounding tur-quoise tinted waters provide the ultimate setting for this record-breaking, albeit tiny island paradise: Both islets are the smallest of the Caribbean dwarf states and also rank among the world’s ten smallest states. A hot pepper sauce, made of a creative mixture of ginger, garlic, thyme and extraordinarily hot chillies that thrive in the hot and humid climate of Nevis, is simmering on the stove of Violet and Llewellyn’s house. Lemmy Pemberton digs up abandoned turtle nests with his bare hands, as he wants to be certain that all of the babies have indeed managed to make it. Members of the Turtle Group catch sea turtles in order to take their measurements and fit them with transmitters. Taxi bus-es are not only the main means of transport on St. Kitts And Nevis, they are also an artistic expression of each driver’s personality. Colourfully embellished, each taxi represents island art on wheels.

programme.title: The Heart of Hawaii - The Island of Oahu
programme.desc: The Oahu island is the economic and cultural centre of the Hawaiian archipelago, as well as being a paradise for surfers, active holidaymakers and freedom lovers. The island is home to more than half of all natives and almost eight million foreign guests annually. Anyone searching for peace and seclusion won’t find either in Honolulu or Waikiki. Traffic congestion and a backdrop of skyscrapers belong to the town panorama. Hip cafes, galleries and young fashion firms have settled here, adding a new and modern flair to the capital. Cindy’s Lei Shoppe, the Chinatown florists, has been here for more than 30 years. This is also because the so-called Leis, the tradition of floral decoration, usually offered as a flower necklace or as a headdress, is still an important part of Hawaiian culture. Keone Nunes is well-known for his traditional tattooing skills, whereby the so-called Kakau Tattoos are virtually hammered into the skin with a hippo tooth. But Oahu is also an island of overwhelming natural beauty and a fascinating diversity on the smallest of places ...

programme.title: The Seychelles - Africa with South Seas ambience
programme.desc: The 115 islands and islets that make up the Seychelles present a breath-taking variety of plants, rare animals and beaches laced with palms. This is where the leg-endary Coco de Mer palm nuts grow with fruits weigh-ing up to 20 kilos and giant wild land turtles nibble away at mangrove fruits to their hearts content. The archipelago was first settled at the end of the 18th cen-tury. Today, a very colourful potpourri of peoples in this dwarf state proves just how peacefully different cultures can live side by side. Three times a week, the steamer MV Espoir completes the trip from the main island of Mahé to Praslin and back. A ship for every-one and practically everything: Used cars, toilet paper, horses, bicycles, furniture - you name it, the Espoir transports goods of all kinds. Coconuts sometimes pose a problem as there are far too many of them. What to do with them? The best place to send them is undoubt-edly Hubert Roumien's Virgin Coconut Oil Laboratory, hidden away in the Mahé jungle. Straw turns into gold at Seaweed Seychelles! There, Benjamin Port Louis collects seaweed and extracts liquid fertiliser from it.

programme.title: Bosnia Herzegovina
programme.desc: Wild and unknown lies the still undiscovered natural paradise of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the heart of Europe. Rough mountains, dense forests and wild waterfalls characterize the picture of the untouched landscapes. Lynx, wolves and bears roam mountains and valleys. One of the last primeval forests in Europe is a retreat for many endangered animal species. Bosnia and Herzegovina is actually an undiscovered natural paradise in the middle of Europe.

programme.title: Bosnia Herzegovina
programme.desc: The barren, karstic south of the country, Herzegovina, also impresses with its natural landscapes. One of them is the Livno field. Not only is it the largest wetland in the country, it is also the largest regularly flooded karst field in the world. About 700 wild horses live in this unique landscape. Their ancestors were working horses that were abandoned here more than 50 years ago. Another special feature of the karst landscape are the rivers with their tufa barriers. The countless waterfalls that pour over it are a unique natural phenomenon.

programme.title: Menorca - Majorca's beautiful sister
programme.desc: Not nearly as crowded as Majorca or Ibiza: Menorca has noticeably fewer visitors than her sister islands and in 1993, was recognised by UNESCO as a biosphere re-serve. Menorca also has its own distinctive charm, with its secluded coves, mighty cliffs, beautiful gardens and ages old towns and villages. Its residents love the is-lands treasures and peculiarities. Forests make up al-most a third of Menorca, complemented by many lush green meadows. Next to tourism, agriculture is a major source of the island's income to the present day. On Menorca, there are several accumulations of enormous megalithic stones. From a global point of view, the up to five-metre-tall Taulas, whereby the stones are ar-ranged in the shape of a T, are unique.

programme.title: Meteor Menace
programme.desc: On February 15th, 2013, out of the blue, a meteorite exploded in the earth’s atmosphere above the Russian region of Chelyabinsk. The event is a reminder of the ever-present 'Meteor Menace' and the need to understand more about these missiles from outer space.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: The Tanzania-Zambia-Railway (Tazara) is one of Africa's most ambitious infrastructure projects. It connects the inland with the coast of East Africa and meant independence from the surrounding apartheid-ruled countries of East Africa. The film accompanies the Tazara on its 52-hour journey through Tanzania and Zambia and uses spectacular aerial shots to show not only the architectural monuments but also the unknown sides of the previously hidden landscapes of Tanzania and Zambia.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: Over 196 bridges and through 55 tunnels, the Bernina Express fights its way from Switzerland to Italy. Powerful forces of nature make the railyway line a dangerous route over the Grisons Alps to this day. The film accompanies the Bernina Express in winter over the highest rail route across the Alps.

programme.title: World's Most Dangerous Railway Lines
programme.desc: The Ferrocarril del Sur, one of the highest train routes on earth, runs right through the mountains of Peru. To this day, it is considered a miracle in the world of railways. The rails not only lead to the famous ruined city of Machu Picchu but connect the ancient Inca capital of Cusco with Puno on the shores of Lake Titicaca and the gleaming white city of Arequipa. A train journey with the Andes Explorer through a grandiose landscape and an undeveloped and inaccessible area.

programme.title: mareTV: Estonia's Enchanted Islands - Kihnu, Hiiumaa, Saaremaa And Co
programme.desc: Kihnu is one of 19 inhabited Estonian islands. When the women there ride motorcycles in colourful skirts, it is summer. Thanks to its remoteness, charming traditions have been preserved here. More than 2,000 islands belong to Estonia, none is like the other, each with its own character. Most of them were military restricted areas during the Soviet Union. Of all things, the strict shielding had its good points: beach, forest, juniper groves, they still characterise the landscape of Estonia's enchanted islands. Elly Karjam is a multi-jobber: lighthouse keeper, ice-cream producer and contract knitter for the famous Kihnu sweaters. Summer is high season for her: She is expecting guests from the USA, who had their ancestors on Kihnu. Birches have to be cut for the so-called viht. This bunch of birch branches is an important accessory for the traditional sauna at midsummer. And the motorcycles in the shed are to be refloated.

programme.title: Secrets of the North Sea
programme.desc: The North Sea is enigmatic. It presents itself in cool shades of grey. Yet who would have guessed that beneath the chilly waves are opulent coral gardens, courting squids, and several of the largest sea creatures on the planet?

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Some risks on these car routes have natural causes: Extreme weather, avalanches and landslides. In some areas, the locals even believe that evil spirits kill travelers. But many of the dangers are man-made: robbers or terrorists lie in wait for travelers, and tough labor pressures, social hardship and greedy mass-transit businesses also cause tragic driving accidents around the world. In the 20th century alone, 35 million people died on roads worldwide - plus 1.5 billion injured!

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Roads are much more than just gray strips of asphalt that allow us to travel and trade. For centuries they have been lifelines of mankind, full of stories and history - and in certain countries and areas they also hold great dangers, much human suffering and death. Documentary filmmaker Oliver G. Becker ventured onto dangerous roads in New Zealand, Scotland and Australia for phoenix.

programme.title: The Moor
programme.desc: Moors and peatlands are oases in the cultivated landscape of Central Europe.

programme.title: Eyes Of The Atacama
programme.desc: ALMA – the Atacama Large Millimeter Array – is the ultimate space observation facility. Here, 66 leviathan parabolic antennae trap cosmic rays in the previously unobservable long-wave range. It can only happen in Atacama, far away from civilisation’s pollution of the night sky with artificial light.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Saguaro National Park is an American national park in Pima County, southeastern Arizona. The 92,000-acre (37,000 ha) park consists of two separate areas—the Tucson Mountain District (TMD) about 10 miles west of the city of Tucson and the Rincon Mountain District (RMD) about 10 miles east of the city—that preserve Sonoran Desert landscapes, fauna, and flora, including the giant saguaro cactus.An inventory of medium and large mammals in the park confirmed the presence of 30 species in Saguaro National Park between 1999 and 2008. Of these, 21 were found in the Tucson Mountain District and 29 in the Rincon Mountain District. A partial list of the park's mammals includes cougars, coyotes, bobcats, white-tailed deer, mule deer, javelinas, gray foxes, black-tailed jackrabbits, desert cottontails, ring-tailed cats, white-nosed coatis, ground squirrels, and packrats. One endangered mammal, the lesser long-nosed bat, lives part of the year in the park and part of the year in Mexico.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Great Smoky Mountains National Park is an American national park in the southeastern United States, with parts in Tennessee and North Carolina. The park straddles the ridgeline of the Great Smoky Mountains, part of the Blue Ridge Mountains, which are a division of the larger Appalachian Mountain chain. The park contains some of the highest mountains in eastern North America, including Clingmans Dome, Mount Guyot, and Mount Le Conte. The border between the two states runs northeast to southwest through the center of the park. The Appalachian Trail passes through the center of the park on its route from Georgia to Maine. With 12.5 million visitors in 2019, the Great Smoky Mountains National Park is the most visited national park in the United States.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Yellowstone National Park is an American national park located in the western United States, largely in the northwest corner of Wyoming and extending into Montana, and Idaho. It was established by the U.S. Congress and signed into law by President Ulysses S. Grant on March 1, 1872. Yellowstone was the first national park in the U.S. and is also widely held to be the first national park in the world. The park is known for its wildlife and its many geothermal features, especially Old Faithful geyser, one of its most popular. While it represents many types of biomes, the subalpine forest is the most abundant. It is part of the South Central Rockies forests ecoregion.

programme.title: The Seychelles - Africa with South Seas ambience
programme.desc: The 115 islands and islets that make up the Seychelles present a breath-taking variety of plants, rare animals and beaches laced with palms. This is where the leg-endary Coco de Mer palm nuts grow with fruits weigh-ing up to 20 kilos and giant wild land turtles nibble away at mangrove fruits to their hearts content. The archipelago was first settled at the end of the 18th cen-tury. Today, a very colourful potpourri of peoples in this dwarf state proves just how peacefully different cultures can live side by side. Three times a week, the steamer MV Espoir completes the trip from the main island of Mahé to Praslin and back. A ship for every-one and practically everything: Used cars, toilet paper, horses, bicycles, furniture - you name it, the Espoir transports goods of all kinds. Coconuts sometimes pose a problem as there are far too many of them. What to do with them? The best place to send them is undoubt-edly Hubert Roumien's Virgin Coconut Oil Laboratory, hidden away in the Mahé jungle. Straw turns into gold at Seaweed Seychelles! There, Benjamin Port Louis collects seaweed and extracts liquid fertiliser from it.

programme.title: mareTV: Capri and the Amalfi Coast - Italy's Ocean Legends
programme.desc: Capri was already in ancient times a place for the rich and beautiful. Today Capri is one of the most famous islands in the world. Millions of tourists visit it. But there are in fact still unknown corners on the island in the Gulf of Naples. Thus, at the very top of Capri, there is a hermit monastery with a view to the Vesuvius.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The racing cyclists of Burundi have a dangerous job. But it’s a vital one for Burundi’s economy. Bicycles are the main means of transportation in one of the smallest countries in Africa. Bananas, the staple food in Burundi, are transported from the markets to a banana beer brewing factory. We accompany Tharcien, a bike courier, on his exhausting cross country trip on the Burundi Highway.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: It is one of the wildest roads in Asia: the Trans Sulawesi Highway. The adventurous road leads through Indonesia's fourth-largest island and takes people to spectacular destinations. To beautiful beaches, turbulent cities, or unique primeval forests.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: Tanzania is known for its national parks, vast landscapes and wild roads. They make traveling a real adventure. We travel in trucks, buses and off-road vehicles from the Indian Ocean via the Serengeti to Lake Victoria, accompany huge herds of wildebeest, observe lions and rhinos - and show the lives of the people who live on and along the roads.

programme.title: Wild Sardinia
programme.desc: Sardinia has always been the epitome of pure wilderness, an emerald of volcanic origin in the Mediterranean. 1900 metres of coastline and an infinite maze of offshore islands. But Sardinia also has other facets: green valleys, rugged mountains, murmuring brooks, mysterious ruins and a unique fauna. Just off of Sardinia's coast is an untouched underwater paradise - uniquely beautiful, but also dangerous. Pilot whales, dolphins and mobula rays populate the waters at Capo Testa in the north of the island. In the west, the lagoons of Cabras represent a wild landscape of lakes in which thousands of flamingos live and hunt the red brine shrimps. In addition to the flamingos, grey and purple herons and little egrets breed here. Thousands of bats have found refuge in the craggy mountain world of the Supramonte and Gennargentu, with their countless grottoes and caves. In the sea we can observe the mass mating of sea slugs, and thanks to our camera robots and submersible boats we were able to observe beard worms with luminous red gills, as well as bright yellow tree corals in the area surrounding the hypothermal lava holes.

programme.title: mareTV: Majorca
programme.desc: Cleaning woman island, concrete castles, Ballermann: Mallorca's image is negatively affected in some respects. The documentary explores the charm of the largest Balearic island beyond the hustle and bustle of tourism and Rambazamba. The real Mallorca is best explored through real Majorcans: Manolo Barahona, TV fishing expert from the local island broadcaster IB3, faces the most difficult task of the year. The Raor is in season, the most expensive fish on the island. Manolo is supposed to get him first in front of the camera and then in the pan. There's only one catch, the little fish with the piranha teeth just doesn't want to be on TV. In the first months of the year Mallorca turns into a sea of almond blossoms. There are around seven million almond trees on the island, once planted to replace dead vines. But now also the almond trees are threatened. The fire bacterium continues to spread, especially on the large plantations. The farmer Biel Torrens wants to save Mallorca's almond trees and fruit with a small organic plantation and gentle harvesting methods. He shakes the almonds from the tree by hand instead of using a mechanical vibrator.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: The contours of the Mediterranean have changed during the course of its history. Near Gibraltar, Africa was once connected to the European continent. When the land bridge at Gibraltar collapsed, the Mediterranean basin filled up again. The Suez Canal is today connected to the Red Sea. This route enables animals to reach the Mediterranean, where they cause problems.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Rugged rocks, blue sea and idyllic, sandy beaches - this is the Mediterranean as we know it. But this impression is deceptive: the Mediterranean is under constant change. The continents are moving towards one another. Animals, that have to survive under such extreme conditions, must find a way to escape the dangers. Between deserts and volcanoes, the challenges for the animals are enormous.

programme.title: mareTV: Scotland's Mild West - On The Inner Hebrides
programme.desc: The Inner Hebrides surprise with green hills, fine sandy beaches and a mild climate, at least as far as Scottish conditions allow. This is ensured by the currents of the Gulf Stream, as well as the Scottish archipelago being protected by its sister islands, which belong to the Outer Hebrides. More than half of the almost 80 islands are uninhabited. Loneliness has made the people rather inventive. On Tiree Island, mathematics, history and physics from the mainland arrive in the classroom per mouseclick. Dr Mauvis Gore and Prof. Rupert Ormond cast off from the island of Mull, after setting a course to encounter a basking shark. The cetohinus maximus is the world's second largest fish and the two scientists are absolutely convinced that the waters surrounding the Mull constitute the mating grounds for the basking sharks. A logistical challenge takes place on the Isle of Easdale each September. Then, around 400 people populate the tiny slate island. Donals Mellon Melville organises the World Skimming Championships, a World Cup in jumping stones. This is all about the distance they are thrown and they must only hop above the water twice.

programme.title: Countries People Adventures - Iceland Extreme
programme.desc: In southeastern Iceland, Europe's largest glacier, the gigantic Vatnajökull, covers an area of around 9,000 square kilometers. Beneath it lie the world's most active and dangerous volcanoes. This extreme landscape is as dangerous as it is fascinating: glistening white glacier tongues, lagoons covered with icebergs, bizarre green lava mountains, snow-covered volcanic cones, solidified lava flows and imposing waterfalls overwhelm everyone who gets to see them. In 2008, Icelanders declared the glacier and adjacent areas a national park, the largest in Europe. In this documentary, the team meets people who live, work or do research here: a life with the dangers of fire and ice in the overwhelming landscape of Vatnajökull National Park.

programme.desc: Expanding practical cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) is nurturing new industries and development opportunities across Central Asia.CGTN speaks with Victoria Khu, co-founder of the SCOLAR Network, and Ulan Abdurazakov, CEO of Nineninesix.ai, to discuss how SCO cooperation shapes young people's education and career paths.

programme.title: From Island Farms to Cloud Power, From Mountain Hubs to Urban Beats
programme.desc: From tropical coffee aromas to high-tech computing hubs, how is China defining high-quality development? In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the fields of Wanning, Hainan, where a small coffee bean becomes a symbol of the Free Trade Port’s opening-up, to the mountains of Guizhou, where a 14-millisecond data latency is powering the rendering of global blockbusters like Ne Zha 2. Finally, we dive into the vibrant Livehouse scene of China’s megacities, exploring a $1.2 billion emotional economy that is reshaping urban nightlife. From solid digital infrastructure to the rhythmic energy of the music scene, this episode captures the heartbeat of China’s evolving economic future.

programme.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programme.desc: China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences.In this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel And Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging AI tourism focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programme.title: The Takaichi Fallout-Behind Japan's Yen Crisis
programme.desc: The yen has plunged to multi-decade lows, prompting a rare coordinated currency intervention by Japan and the United States. Meanwhile, U.S. Treasury yields are surging, with the 30-year yield reaching its highest level since 2007.What is driving the yen’s weakness？Is Japan’s yen crisis becoming a global bond-market story? Join us on BizTalk as we examine Japan’s economic challenges, #TheTakaichiFallout and the global risks behind the latest bond-market sell-off.

programme.title: New consumption scenes: Exploring Suzhou's lotus market with a foreign vlogger
programme.desc: Cherry Qiu and foreign vlogger Wang Dehua visited the famous Taohuawu Lotus Market in Suzhou, and savored the Su‑style lifestyle. This livestream showcases how traditional Chinese culture thrives in modern consumption scenarios, and how Suzhou leverages its distinctive cultural resources to create new inbound‑tourism experiences marked by greater interactivity, immersive engagement and international appeal.

programme.title: Observing Europe-So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems

programme.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programme.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing...

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration weaponized in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested.The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure.From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programme.title: From Island Farms to Cloud Power, From Mountain Hubs to Urban Beats
programme.desc: From tropical coffee aromas to high-tech computing hubs, how is China defining high-quality development? In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the fields of Wanning, Hainan, where a small coffee bean becomes a symbol of the Free Trade Port’s opening-up, to the mountains of Guizhou, where a 14-millisecond data latency is powering the rendering of global blockbusters like Ne Zha 2. Finally, we dive into the vibrant Livehouse scene of China’s megacities, exploring a $1.2 billion emotional economy that is reshaping urban nightlife. From solid digital infrastructure to the rhythmic energy of the music scene, this episode captures the heartbeat of China’s evolving economic future.

programme.title: Observing Europe-So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems
programme.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programme.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programme.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing...

programme.title: Observing Europe - Is migration weaponized in Europe?
programme.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested.The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure.From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. programme.title: Escape to Yibin
programme.desc: Yibin is hailed as The First City along the Yangtze River, home to renowned Yibin Ranmian noodles and Wuliangye liquor.We explored plenty of lesser-known scenic spots: Lizhuang, the cultural hub during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression; vast bamboo groves that embody the hermit culture of China; and the mysterious cliff-hanging coffins.It is precisely these secluded and strategically advantageous lands that enabled local cultures to be well preserved amid turbulent times.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China : Shanghai
programme.desc: Balancing delicately on an alluvial plain and the Yangtze estuary of China’s east coast, much of Shanghai-literally meaning “on the sea”-sits at an average sea-level elevation of about 4 meters. Bisecting the city is the Huangpu River, dividing it into Puxi (west bank) and Pudong (east bank), where you’ll find its famous international airport. Join us as on an aerial cruise as we journey upstream towards one of the world’s most recognizable skylines.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-3 Shaolin Style
programme.desc: Episode 3, Shaolin, explores how this thousand-year-old temple has evolved into a unique “kung fu platform” that draws enthusiasts from around the world. Host Kleber immerses himself in Shaolin’s integrated way of life, where Chan (Zen) practice and martial training go hand in hand, and turns the camera toward foreign practitioners pursuing their kung fu dreams both inside and beyond the temple gates.Along the way, he meets international disciples living and training at Shaolin, as well as students learning the rare art of Shaolin Xinyiba under Master Hu Zhengsheng, a former Shaolin monk. At martial arts schools near Songshan Mountain, Kleber also encounters overseas competitors training...

programme.title: Foodwise: Datong
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Angela Fu are in historic Datong. Located in northern China's Shanxi Province, some 1500 years ago Datong was the capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty, which saw nomads unite northern China and Buddhism spread throughout the country. At the renowned Yungang Grottoes where giant Buddhas were carved out of cliffs, our hosts discover Datong's multicultural past and sample the emperor's favorite cake. They seek out the remains of a Jesuit church beneath the Great Wall of China, and find in the local cuisine elements that echo the past, and modern-day recipes for thousand-year old dishes.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chaozhou
programme.desc: In this episode, hosts Tianran He and Angela Fu are in Chaozhou, South China. They're on a quest to discover the secrets of its success, for Chaozhou is famed for its wealthy merchant guilds and its homegrown Teochew cuisine, which enjoys global recognition.From working as part-timers in a beef hotpot restaurant, to learning about tea ceremony and shadowing a master of Teochew cuisine, our hosts discover the best way to learn about Chaozhou, is through its food.

They're on a quest to discover the secrets of its success, for Chaozhou is famed for its wealthy merchant guilds and its homegrown Teochew cuisine, which enjoys global recognition.From working as part-timers in a beef hotpot restaurant, to learning about tea ceremony and shadowing a master of Teochew cuisine, our hosts discover the best way to learn about Chaozhou, is through its food.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-3 Shaolin Style
programme.desc: Episode 3, Shaolin, explores how this thousand-year-old temple has evolved into a unique “kung fu platform” that draws enthusiasts from around the world. Host Kleber immerses himself in Shaolin’s integrated way of life, where Chan (Zen) practice and martial training go hand in hand, and turns the camera toward foreign practitioners pursuing their kung fu dreams both inside and beyond the temple gates.Along the way, he meets international disciples living and training at Shaolin, as well as students learning the rare art of Shaolin Xinyiba under Master Hu Zhengsheng, a former Shaolin monk. At martial arts schools near Songshan Mountain, Kleber also encounters overseas competitors training...

programme.title: China Bound: Harbin
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Harbin, the Ice City, host of the 2025 Asian Winter Games. Internationally renowned for its breathtaking ice and snow sculptures, the city thrives with activity despite it -20°C winters. From savoring the famous local ice cream and hearty northeastern Chinese dishes such as stewed goose and sweet-and-sour pork, to drifting on the frozen Songhua River and carving down the slopse of Yabuli Ski Resort, discover how much fun you can have in Harbin.

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview the Monkey Father—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. programme.title: 240-Hour Pass in China: Where Pavilions Meet Peaks
programme.desc: Meaning south of the lake and north of the lake, the provinces of Hunan and Hubei in central China take their names from their positions around Dongting Lake – China's second-largest freshwater lake. Nestled along the middle reaches of the Yangtze River, these two provinces are blessed with stunning landscapes and rich local traditions. From the legendary Yellow Crane Tower in Hubei to the breathtaking peaks of Zhangjiajie in Hunan, this journey through central China promises beauty, culture and adventure at every turn. Join CGTN reporter Lucy Lü as she steps into ancient pavilions, uncovers treasured relics, climbs soaring mountains and wanders through riverside towns where tradition...

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China.In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui...

programme.title: Escape to Yibin
programme.desc: Yibin is hailed as The First City along the Yangtze River, home to renowned Yibin Ranmian noodles and Wuliangye liquor.We explored plenty of lesser-known scenic spots: Lizhuang, the cultural hub during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression; vast bamboo groves that embody the hermit culture of China; and the mysterious cliff-hanging coffins.It is precisely these secluded and strategically advantageous lands that enabled local cultures to be well preserved amid turbulent times.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China : Shanghai
programme.desc: Balancing delicately on an alluvial plain and the Yangtze estuary of China’s east coast, much of Shanghai-literally meaning “on the sea”-sits at an average sea-level elevation of about 4 meters. Bisecting the city is the Huangpu River, dividing it into Puxi (west bank) and Pudong (east bank), where you’ll find its famous international airport. Join us as on an aerial cruise as we journey upstream towards one of the world’s most recognizable skylines.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chongqing
programme.desc: Welcome to Chongqing, China's largest city. Located in the country's southwest, it straddles two mighty rivers and is famed for its extraordinary skyline, with high-rises mushrooming out of the hills and vertigo-inducing bridges.But Tianran He and Angela Fu are here for the food: From xiaomian noodles and Jianghu cuisine to the city's most famous dish: Chongqing hotpot, our hosts take on the spicy, numbing and scintillating aromas of Chongqing cuisine. We promise you: Chongqing will electrify your senses and tantalise your taste buds.

programme.title: Foodwise: Veggie Beijing
programme.desc: Beijing is a 3000-year old metropolis home to a dizzying array of culinary traditions, not least of which is vegetarian cuisine. For Beijingers, eating vegetarian is the best way to welcome spring. In this episode, Tianran and Angela take up the challenge: From simple home cooking utilizing spring flowers and leaves, to the extravagant mock-meat masterpieces of imperial cuisine, and international dishes well-known to the vegetarian community, our hosts discover a plethora of plant-based options to be found amongst the historic alleys and skyscrapers of China's capital.

programme.desc: CGTN’s integrated media cultural and travel program China Untapped: Suzhou features industrial tourism as its core theme, complemented by Jiangnan cultural tourism. programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune!

programme.title: Beijing Unboxed: More Than Palaces
programme.desc: When you think of Beijing, what comes to mind? The Forbidden City, the Summer Palace, the Great Wall, the Temple of Heaven? These iconic landmarks tell the story of a city with over 3,000 years of history. But Beijing isn't just about the past. It's a vibrant, ever-changing metropolis. Join travel vloggers Lucy and Ioana as they skip the usual tourist spots and show you a side of Beijing where history, modern life, and creativity meet.

programme.title: The Spirit of Zhaxidele
programme.desc: In this episode of Travelogue, Tianran backpacks the way to the western reaches of China. Making his home in beautiful Jiaju village, he learns just what it takes to be a Tibetan, then reaches the mysterious village of Suopo and explore its ancient watchtowers.

programme.title: China Highly Recommended: Changsha
programme.desc: Episode 1 of Travelogue's China Highly Recommended tells the story of Changsha, one of China's happiest cities. Following the lives of four of its foreign residents: A French executive chef, a Japanese podcaster, and two American teachers, we discover the reasons why they made Changsha their second home, and explore the city with them as only locals do. This episode will be released as a 30 minute travel documentary to be broadcast on CGTN's television channel and social media platform, along with a series of video clips and photos

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media – Changsha was China's first UNESCO Creative City. It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune!

programme.title: The Spirit of Zhaxidele
programme.desc: In this episode of Travelogue, Tianran backpacks the way to the western reaches of China. Making his home in beautiful Jiaju village, he learns just what it takes to be a Tibetan, then reaches the mysterious village of Suopo and explore its ancient watchtowers.

The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chongqing
programme.desc: Welcome to Chongqing, China's largest city. Located in the country's southwest, it straddles two mighty rivers and is famed for its extraordinary skyline, with high-rises mushrooming out of the hills and vertigo-inducing bridges.But Tianran He and Angela Fu are here for the food: From xiaomian noodles and Jianghu cuisine to the city's most famous dish: Chongqing hotpot, our hosts take on the spicy, numbing and scintillating aromas of Chongqing cuisine. We promise you: Chongqing will electrify your senses and tantalise your taste buds.

programme.title: Foodwise: Veggie Beijing
programme.desc: Beijing is a 3000-year old metropolis home to a dizzying array of culinary traditions, not least of which is vegetarian cuisine. For Beijingers, eating vegetarian is the best way to welcome spring. In this episode, Tianran and Angela take up the challenge: From simple home cooking utilizing spring flowers and leaves, to the extravagant mock-meat masterpieces of imperial cuisine, and international dishes well-known to the vegetarian community, our hosts discover a plethora of plant-based options to be found amongst the historic alleys and skyscrapers of China's capital.

programme.title: Beijing Unboxed: More Than Palaces
programme.desc: When you think of Beijing, what comes to mind? The Forbidden City, the Summer Palace, the Great Wall, the Temple of Heaven? These iconic landmarks tell the story of a city with over 3,000 years of history. But Beijing isn't just about the past. It's a vibrant, ever-changing metropolis. Join travel vloggers Lucy and Ioana as they skip the usual tourist spots and show you a side of Beijing where history, modern life, and creativity meet.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-4 Medieval Combat
programme.desc: Episode 4 centres on Shanghai, where Eastern and Western martial traditions meet in surprising ways. Kleber visits local practitioners of Historical European Martial Arts (HEMA), trying German and Italian longsword techniques first-hand and seeing how Chinese enthusiasts innovate by combining European swordsmanship with ancient Chinese military manuals.The episode also follows the rise of BUHURT, a European-style armored combat sport now gaining traction in China, featuring locally made traditional Chinese armour in intense full-contact bouts. programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-5 Xingyi Quan
programme.desc: In Episode 5, Kleber travels to Shanxi, the birthplace of Xingyi Quan. He follows Master Cao Bing, a traditional Xingyi Quan teacher and modern combat coach, from Taiyuan’s noodle shops to Pingyao’s ancient streets, and from centuries-old vinegar breweries to Guandi temples, exploring Xingyi Quan’s deep links to Shanxi’s merchant culture and history.Master Cao breaks down the core principles of the “Five Elements and Twelve Forms”, and shows in his modern gym how techniques found in Muay Thai and Jiu-Jitsu can be integrated without losing Xingyi Quan’s philosophical core, guided by the mindset of taking only what is essential.
